chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bakeyr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who gives charity: Is it permissible for him to retract his charity? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Charity is a newly occurring concept; rather, it was al-Nuhl (gifts given before possession) and al-Hibah (gifts given after possession). And for the one who gives a gift or a donation, it is permissible to retract it whether he has taken possession or not. And it is not befitting for the one who gives something for the sake of Allah to retract it.'

key_terms.النُّحْل: Gifts given before the recipient takes possession
key_terms.الْهِبَة: Gifts given after the recipient takes possession

ai.seo_question: Can a person take back their charity (sadaqah) after giving it?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while gifts (hibah) are revocable regardless of possession, charity (sadaqah) given for Allah’s sake is considered a permanent endowment, reflecting the principle that one who gives to God should not take back. This distinction underscores the spiritual gravity of sadaqah in Shia jurisprudence, elevating it above mere transactional gift-giving. The ruling highlights the ethical expectation of steadfastness in charitable acts dedicated to divine pleasure.
